summary: Documents the extensions to SDP and RTSP that 3GPP's Packet-switched Streaming Service and Multimedia Broadcast/Multicast Service use, and registers them with IANA. It is informational.

eli5.summary: Mobile phone video services use some special extra words in streaming messages. This writes those words down and registers them.

subtitle: SDP and RTSP extensions that 3GPP uses for mobile video streaming and broadcast services.

tldr.problem: 3GPP's mobile streaming services (Packet-switched Streaming Service and Multimedia Broadcast/Multicast Service) need extensions to the Session Description Protocol (SDP) and Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) to describe and control video quality, buffering, error correction, and content protection features specific to mobile networks.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6064 documents the SDP attributes and RTSP headers and option tags that 3GPP defined for these services, and registers them with IANA to avoid conflicts and raise awareness.
tldr.outcome: The extensions are now formally registered with IANA, so other standards bodies can reference them. The normative specifications remain in 3GPP technical standards documents, which can evolve independently.

facts.label: Services covered
facts.value: PSS and MBMS for mobile video streaming

facts.label: SDP extensions
facts.value: Buffering, security, alternatives, QoE metrics, adaptation, FEC repair

facts.label: RTSP extensions
facts.value: Link info, adaptation, QoE, video buffer, integrity, stream switching

today: RFC 6064 is an Informational RFC published in January 2011. It documents 3GPP-defined extensions to SDP and RTSP as of Release 7. It remains the reference for IANA registrations, although 3GPP continues to enhance these services in later releases. Change control of the extensions belongs to 3GPP, not IETF.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
3GPP, the standards body for mobile telecommunications, has defined two major services that use video streaming:

  • Packet-switched Streaming Service (PSS): a unicast streaming service for on-demand or live video delivered to mobile phones.
  • Multimedia Broadcast/Multicast Service (MBMS): a broadcast and multicast service for delivering content to many mobile terminals at once.

Both services use the standard Session Description Protocol (SDP) to describe multimedia sessions and the Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) to control playback. However, mobile networks have constraints not present on fixed networks: variable bandwidth, buffering requirements, battery life concerns, and content protection needs. To address these, 3GPP extended SDP and RTSP with new attributes and headers. RFC 6064 documents these extensions and registers them with IANA.
sections.eli5: Phone companies use SDP and RTSP for video, but phones have special needs like limited battery and changing network speed. So they added extra settings to those standards.

sections.title: SDP Extensions for Streaming Services
sections.content:
SDP is used to describe what media is available in a session. 3GPP added many attributes at both session and media level:

Video buffering attributes tell the receiver how much data to buffer before starting playback, how long to buffer initially, and the peak decoding rate. Examples include a=X-predecbufsize and a=X-initpredecbufperiod. These help prevent underflow when network data arrives unevenly.

Integrity protection attributes like a=3GPP-Integrity-Key and a=3GPP-SRTP-Config enable encryption and authentication of the SDP and media.

Alternative attributes allow the server to provide multiple alternative SDP configurations (for example, different bitrates or languages) and let the client choose one that fits its capabilities and preferences.

Quality of Experience (QoE) metrics enable measurement and reporting of the quality perceived by the user.

Adaptation and asset information attributes support dynamic adjustment of streaming bitrate and metadata like title and description.

For MBMS, which uses multicast, 3GPP added attributes for Forward Error Correction (FEC) and bearer mode declaration.
sections.eli5: Attributes in SDP are like a recipe for the video player. 3GPP added instructions for buffering, protecting the stream, offering choices, measuring quality, and fixing errors that happen in broadcast.

sections.title: RTSP Extensions for Streaming
sections.content:
RTSP is the protocol for controlling streaming: starting, pausing, and stopping playback. 3GPP added new RTSP headers to communicate QoS information and streaming parameters between client and server.

3GPP-Link-Char header is sent by the mobile client to tell the server about the wireless link: guaranteed bandwidth, maximum bandwidth, and maximum delay. The server can use this to choose an appropriate bitrate.

3GPP-Adaptation header lets the client tell the server about its buffer size and desired target time, enabling the server to adapt the bitrate to avoid buffer underflow or overflow.

3GPP-QoE-Metrics and 3GPP-QoE-Feedback headers allow the client to report metrics about the quality experienced: latency, frame rate, packet loss, and so on.

Video buffer headers like x-predecbufsize are sent in PLAY responses to inform the client about buffer configuration.

Fast startup and content switching headers added in later releases (Switch-Stream, SDP-Requested, Pipelined-Requests) allow clients to switch to new content without breaking and restarting the RTSP session, reducing channel-switching delay.

Integrity protection uses the 3GPP-Freshness-Token header to prevent replay attacks.
sections.eli5: When a phone plays video, the server and phone exchange RTSP messages. 3GPP added messages where the phone tells the server 'my connection is slow' and the server says 'okay, lower the bitrate', and messages for the phone to report how good the picture is.

sections.title: IANA Registration and Maintenance
sections.content:
The main purpose of RFC 6064 is to formally register these extensions with IANA so they have stable definitions and to alert the IETF community to their existence. The normative definitions of these extensions remain in 3GPP technical specification documents (such as TS 26.234 for PSS and TS 26.346 for MBMS).

This arrangement allows 3GPP to update and enhance these extensions in future releases without waiting for an IETF RFC process. However, to keep the IETF informed of significant changes, IANA should be notified when references are updated, and preferably a new version of RFC 6064 or an updated RFC should be published.

For the SDP protocol identifiers used in MBMS FEC (forward error correction), such as UDP/MBMS-FEC/RTP/AVP, RFC 6064 provides the normative definitions since these require an IETF RFC.

The registrations include SDP attributes, RTSP headers, and RTSP option tags. Each registration includes a reference to the relevant section of the 3GPP specification so that implementers can find the full definition.
sections.eli5: This document says to the Internet standards body: 'Here are the names 3GPP is using for these extensions. Write them down so nobody else uses the same names, and so people know where to find the details.'

items.title: Buffering
items.text: Attributes that tell the player how much to buffer and for how long before starting playback.

items.title: Security
items.text: Encryption keys and SRTP configuration for protecting the stream from eavesdropping.

items.title: Alternatives
items.text: Multiple SDP configurations at different bitrates or in different languages for the client to choose.

items.title: Quality Metrics
items.text: Parameters to measure and report the user's experience of the video quality.

items.title: Adaptation
items.text: Support for adjusting the streaming bitrate dynamically based on network conditions.

items.title: Error Correction
items.text: FEC configuration for MBMS broadcast to recover from lost packets.
